- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or volatile (alternating ±0.33), model often underestimates or overshoots mid-cycle; apply mean reversion bias toward recent 7-day average.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast peak at 10% above prior high.
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., 1.00 → -0.33 → 1.00), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment weight to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in cycle; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per 5-day window if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price declines (e.g., 1.00 → 0.33 → 0.00), model overreacts; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3 days.
